question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'** i.e.** 'What'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct option to fill in blank number 3 is **"what".**
 
• The word** "what" **is used here as a pronoun to introduce a clause specifying something.
 
• **In this context**, the word "what" makes sense because it is asking the reader to consider the intentions or desires of sellers and other users on social media platforms.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *Social media platforms and many people on them have their own agendas and they are often trying to sell you things. So, be aware of how much time and energy you give to sellers and users and think about **what **they want from you when engaging. To gauge which uses are positive and (4) ______ and which are detrimental, ask yourself simply, when does using social media make me feel good or bad, and why? Do I (5) ______use it all of the time?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at why the other options are not correct:
 
 
• **"That" **- This word can be used as a relative pronoun to introduce a clause, but in this case, it doesn't fit well because we are trying to introduce a clause specifying something rather than defining or identifying it.
 
• **"Whilst" **- This is a formal equivalent to "while," but it doesn't fit in this context because it introduces a time-related or contrasting clause, not a clause specifying something.
 
• **"Which" **- This word is used as a relative pronoun to introduce non-defining relative clauses. In this sentence, we need to introduce a clause specifying something, not providing additional information about it.
